```{r}
#| label: pipeline
# Shared setup for every section: load, clean, split, recipe, prep
library(pacman)
p_load(tidyverse, tidymodels, here, gt, GGally)
tidymodels_prefer()

# load data
phones <- here("data/smartphone_cleaned_v5.csv") |>
read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE)
```

```{r}
# 1. Data Cleaning
# - remove the 2 luxury editions where their price comes from gold/materials
# - perform transformation, log the price as it is heavily right-skewed
# - recode 5G and NFC to Yes/No so the dummy names are readable
# - keeps the 7 biggest brands, pool the rest into "Other", and make "xiaomi" the base reference level.
# - keeps only the 12 variables used, then drop incomplete rows.
pca_vars <- c("processor_speed", "ram_capacity", "internal_memory",
              "refresh_rate", "primary_camera_rear", "primary_camera_front")

phones_clean <- phones |>
  filter(!model %in% c("Vertu Signature Touch", 
                       "Xiaomi Redmi K20 Pro Signature Edition")) |>
  mutate(
    log_price = log(price),
    has_5g = factor(if_else(as.logical(has_5g), "Yes", "No"), 
                    levels = c("No", "Yes")),
    has_nfc = factor(if_else(as.logical(has_nfc), "Yes", "No"),
                     levels = c("No", "Yes")),
    brand_group = fct_relevel(fct_lump_n(brand_name, n = 7), "xiaomi")
  ) |>
  select(log_price, all_of(pca_vars), battery_capacity, screen_size, has_5g,
         has_nfc, brand_group) |>
  na.omit()
```

```{r}
# 2. Split: 75% training, 25% testing
set.seed(41352)
phone_split <- initial_split(phones_clean, prop = 0.75, strata = log_price)
phone_training <- training(phone_split)
phone_test <- testing(phone_split)
```

```{r}
# 3. Recipe: normalise -> PCA on the 6 specifications -> dummy variables -> drop constants
phone_rec <- recipe(log_price ~ ., data = phone_training) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
  step_pca(all_of(pca_vars), threshold = 0.7, id = "pca") |>
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_zv(all_predictors())
```

```{r}
# 4. Prep
phone_prep <- prep(phone_rec)
```

# Data preparation and PCA {background-color="#1F4E79"}

```{r}
#| label: corr-numbers
# Numbers used in the text of this slide
nice_names <- c(
  processor_speed = "Processor speed",
  ram_capacity = "RAM",
  internal_memory = "Internal memory",
  refresh_rate = "Refresh rate",
  primary_camera_rear = "Rear camera",
  primary_camera_front = "Front camera"
)

pca_data <- phones_clean |>
  select(all_of(pca_vars))

# Full correlation table for heatmap
cor_full <- cor(pca_data) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  rownames_to_column("v1") |>
  pivot_longer(-v1, names_to = "v2", values_to = "r") |>
  mutate(v1 = unname(nice_names[v1]),
         v2 = unname(nice_names[v2]))

# One copy of each pair (v1 < v2) for the strongest and weakest pair
cor_long <- cor_full |>
  filter(v1 < v2)

top_pair <- slice_max(cor_long, r, n = 1)
low_pair <- slice_min(cor_long, r, n = 1)
mean_r <- mean(cor_long$r)
```

## Are the specifications correlated? {.smaller}

:::::::: columns
::: {.column width="58%"}
```{r}
#| label: fig-corr
#| fig-cap: "Correlations among the six specifications used in the PCA."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6
pca_data |>
  rename_with(~ unname(nice_names[.x])) |>
  ggpairs(upper = list(continuous = wrap("cor", size = 6)),
          lower = list(continuous = wrap("points", size = 0.4, alpha = 0.3))) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12)
```
:::

:::::: {.column width="42%"}
::: incremental
- **Correlations** range from `r round(low_pair$r, 2)` to `r round(top_pair$r, 2)`, with an average of `r round(mean_r, 2)`.

- **Strongest pair:** `r top_pair$v1` and `r top_pair$v2` (`r round(top_pair$r, 2)`); **weakest:** `r low_pair$v1` and `r low_pair$v2` (`r round(low_pair$r, 2)`).

- The specifications **overlap**, so **PCA** can combine them into **fewer** uncorrelated components.
:::

:::: fragment
::: {.callout-tip title="So what"}
Phones can be compared on a few overall specification levels instead of six separate numbers.
:::
::::
::::::
::::::::

::: notes
The scatter plot matrix is the evidence that PCA suits the data. If the variables were unrelated, PCA would not be able to summarise them.
:::

## Data preparation {.smaller}

```{r}
#| label: prep-numbers
n_raw   <- nrow(phones)
n_clean <- nrow(phones_clean)
n_miss  <- n_raw - 2 - n_clean
```

:::::::: columns
::: {.column width="40%"}
```{r}
#| label: tbl-prep
#| tbl-cap: "Smartphones at each preparation step."
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom
tibble(
  step = c(
    "Original dataset",
    "Luxury editions removed",
    "Incomplete records removed",
    "Used in the analysis",
    "Training set (75%)",
    "Testing set (25%)"
  ),
  smartphones = c(n_raw, 2, n_miss, n_clean, nrow(phone_training), nrow(phone_test))
) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(step = "Step", smartphones = "Smartphones") |>
  opt_table_outline() |>
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(18),
              column_labels.font.weight = "bold",
              column_labels.vlines.style = "solid",
              table_body.vlines.style = "solid")
```
:::

:::: {.column width="60%"}
::: incremental
- **`r n_clean` of `r n_raw`** phones used (@tbl-prep)

- **Luxury editions** (2) removed: priced for materials, not specifications.

- **Incomplete records** removed: PCA cannot handle missing values.

- **Price** logged (strongly right-skewed); **brand** grouped into the top 7 plus Other.

- **5G** and **NFC** recoded to No/Yes; **Xiaomi** is the base brand for comparison.
:::
::::

:::: fragment
::: {.callout-tip title="So what"}
The results describe how specifications relate to price for typical smartphones.
:::
::::
::::::::

::: notes
Price was logged because it is strongly right-skewed. Luxury editions were removed because their prices only reflect gold and premium materials.
:::

## Method and justification {.smaller}

| Choice | Reason |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| **PCA** on six specifications | Specifications overlap (@fig-corr); a few uncorrelated components avoid multicollinearity. |
| **Standardise** before PCA | Units differ (GB, GHz, Hz, MP); stops variables with large-number from dominating. |
| **Linear regression** | Log price is numeric; the question is what drives price. |
| **Variables left out** | Rating: largely explained by the specifications. Fast charging: missing for most iPhones. |

::: notes
Normalise comes before the dummy step so that the 0/1 dummy variables are not rescaled.
:::

## Preprocessing steps {.smaller}

::: {.fragment .fade-in-then-semi-out}
1.  **Standardise** all numeric predictors.
    - Fair weighting in PCA.
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-in-then-semi-out}
2.  **Combine** the six specifications into **principal components** that explain at least 70% of the variance.
    - Removes overlap and keeps key information.
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-in-then-semi-out}
3.  Turn 5G, NFC and brand into 0/1 **dummy variables.**
    - Regression requires numbers; done after standardising so they stay 0/1.
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-in-then-semi-out}
4.  **Drop** any **column** with a **single value**.
    - Avoids useless predictors.
:::

## Variance explained {.smaller}

```{r}
#| label: var-numbers
var_tbl <- tidy(phone_prep, id = "pca", type = "variance")

# number of components kept = number of PC columns after bake()
n_pc <- bake(phone_prep, new_data = NULL) |>
  select(starts_with("PC")) |>
  ncol()

pc1_var <- var_tbl |>
  filter(terms == "percent variance", component == 1) |>
  pull(value)

cum_var <- var_tbl |>
  filter(terms == "cumulative percent variance", component == n_pc) |>
  pull(value)

# variance of the first component that is not kept
next_var <- var_tbl |>
  filter(terms == "percent variance", component == n_pc + 1) |>
  pull(value)

var_wide <- var_tbl |>
  filter(terms %in% c("percent variance", "cumulative percent variance")) |>
  select(component, terms, value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = terms, values_from = value) |>
  mutate(component = paste0("PC", component))
```

::::: columns
::: {.column width="45%"}
```{r}
#| label: tbl-var
#| tbl-cap: "Variance explained by each principal component."
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom
var_wide |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(component = "Component",
             `percent variance` = "Variance (%)",
             `cumulative percent variance` = "Cumulative (%)") |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(`percent variance`, `cumulative percent variance`),
             decimals = 1) |>
  opt_table_outline() |>
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(18),
              column_labels.font.weight = "bold",
              column_labels.vlines.style = "solid",
              table_body.vlines.style = "solid")
```
:::

::: {.column width="55%"}
```{r}
#| label: fig-scree
#| fig-cap: "Percentage of variance explained by each component."
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 6
ggplot(var_wide, aes(component, `percent variance`)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2C7FB8") +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(`percent variance`, 1)), vjust = -0.4) +
  labs(x = "Component", y = "Percentage of variance") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 16)
```
:::
:::::

::: notes
Percent variance is the share of the total information that each component holds. PC1 always holds the most.
:::

## Number of components retained {.smaller}

::: incremental
- **PC1** explains **`r round(pc1_var, 1)`%** of the variance in the six specifications (@tbl-var, @fig-scree).

- The first **`r n_pc` PCs** together explain **`r round(cum_var, 1)`%**, meeting the **70% threshold**.

- Each remaining component adds only **`r round(next_var, 1)`% or less**.
:::

. . .

::: {.callout-tip title="So what"}
**`r n_pc` PCs are kept:** each phone is described by `r n_pc` components instead of six specifications, with little loss of information.
:::

::: notes
The 70% threshold is set in step_pca(). R keeps the smallest number of components whose cumulative variance reaches 70%.
:::

```{r}
#| label: fit-model
#| output: false

linear_model <- linear_reg() |>
  set_engine("lm") |>
  set_mode("regression")

phone_wkfl <- workflow() |>
  add_model(linear_model) |>
  add_recipe(phone_rec)

phone_fit <- phone_wkfl |>
  fit(data = phone_training)

phone_results <- phone_fit |>
  extract_fit_parsnip() |>
  tidy() |>
  mutate(significance = case_when(p.value < 0.001 ~ "0.1%",
                                  p.value < 0.01 ~ "1%",
                                  p.value < 0.05 ~ "5%",
                                  TRUE ~ "Not significant"),
         # readable names for the slides
         label = case_when(term == "(Intercept)" ~ "Intercept",
                           term == "battery_capacity" ~ "Battery capacity",
                           term == "screen_size" ~ "Screen size",
                           term == "PC1" ~ "PC1: overall performance",
                           term == "PC2" ~ "PC2: storage and speed vs camera",
                           term == "has_5g_Yes" ~ "5G (vs no 5G)",
                           term == "has_nfc_Yes" ~ "NFC (vs no NFC)",
                           term == "brand_group_apple" ~ "Apple",
                           term == "brand_group_motorola" ~ "Motorola",
                           term == "brand_group_oppo" ~ "Oppo",
                           term == "brand_group_realme" ~ "Realme",
                           term == "brand_group_samsung" ~ "Samsung",
                           term == "brand_group_vivo" ~ "Vivo",
                           term == "brand_group_Other" ~ "Other brands"))

# the 7 brand dummies (each compared with Xiaomi, the base category)
brand_terms <- c("brand_group_apple", "brand_group_motorola", "brand_group_oppo",
                 "brand_group_realme", "brand_group_samsung", "brand_group_vivo",
                 "brand_group_Other")
```

```{r}
#| label: base-levels
#| output: false
# base category = first level of each factor
levels(phones_clean$has_5g)
levels(phones_clean$has_nfc)
levels(phones_clean$brand_group)
```

# Regression Results {background-color="#1f4e79"}

## What drives smartphone prices? {.smaller}

Dependent variable: **log price**. Base categories: **Xiaomi**, **no 5G**, **no NFC**. We read the **significance level** and the **sign** only, not the size of each coefficient.

:::::: columns
::: {.column width="55%"}
```{r}
#| label: tbl-specs
#| tbl-cap: "Components, specifications and features"
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom
phone_results |>
  filter(!term %in% brand_terms) |>
  select(label, estimate, p.value, significance) |>
  mutate(estimate = round(estimate, 3), p.value = round(p.value, 4)) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(columns = p.value, decimals = 4) |>
  cols_label(label = "Term", estimate = "Coefficient",
             p.value = "p-value", significance = "Significance") |>
  cols_align(align = "center", columns = c(p.value, significance)) |>
  opt_table_outline() |>
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(18),
              column_labels.font.weight = "bold",
              column_labels.vlines.style = "solid",
              table_body.vlines.style = "solid")
```
:::

::: {.column width="3%"}
:::

::: {.column width="42%"}
```{r}
#| label: tbl-brands
#| tbl-cap: "Brands compared with Xiaomi"
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom
phone_results |>
  filter(term %in% brand_terms) |>
  select(label, estimate, p.value, significance) |>
  mutate(estimate = round(estimate, 3), p.value = round(p.value, 4)) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(columns = p.value, decimals = 4) |>
  cols_label(label = "Brand", estimate = "Coefficient",
             p.value = "p-value", significance = "Significance") |>
  cols_align(align = "center", columns = c(p.value, significance)) |>
  opt_table_outline() |>
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(18),
              column_labels.font.weight = "bold",
              column_labels.vlines.style = "solid",
              table_body.vlines.style = "solid")
```
:::
::::::

::: notes
Linear regression fitted on the training data with the tidymodels workflow. As the brief asks, we only fit and interpret the model; we do not evaluate its fit or prediction. A positive sign means a higher log price, and so a higher price.
:::

## Specifications vs price {.smaller}

::: incremental
- **Overall performance (PC1):** **positive significant influence** on price at the **0.1% level** (@tbl-specs); stronger all-round phones are priced higher.
- **Storage and speed vs camera (PC2):** **positive significant influence** at the **0.1% level**; storage- and speed-focused phones are priced higher than camera-focused ones.
- **Screen size:** **positive significant influence** at the **0.1% level**; larger screens, higher price.
- **Battery capacity:** **negative significant influence** at the **0.1% level**; larger batteries, lower price.
:::

. . .

::: {.callout-tip title="So what"}
Price follows the performance bundle and screen size, not battery size or camera megapixels alone.
:::

::: notes
All four effects hold after taking the other variables in the model into account. PC1 and PC2 are named from their loadings on the previous slides. PC1: processor, RAM, storage, refresh rate and both cameras all load positively, so a higher PC1 means a stronger all-round phone. PC2: storage and processor load positively and the two cameras negatively, so among phones with similar overall performance, a higher PC2 means a storage- and speed-focused phone. Large batteries are a main selling point of budget phones, which likely explains the negative sign.
:::

## Features and brands vs price {.smaller}

```{r}
#| label: brand-data
#| output: false
brand_results <- phone_results |>
  filter(term %in% brand_terms)
```

:::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
#| label: fig-brand
#| fig-cap: "Brand coefficients compared with Xiaomi (teal = significant at 5%, red = not significant)"
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 5
brand_results |>
  ggplot(aes(label, estimate, fill = p.value < 0.05)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = "Brand", y = "Coefficient (log price) vs Xiaomi") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 16)
```
:::

:::: {.column width="50%"}
::: fragment
- Phones **with NFC:** significantly **higher** price than without NFC (0.1% level).
- Phones **with 5G:** significantly **higher** price than without 5G (5% level).
- **Apple, Samsung** (0.1%) and **Vivo** (1%): significantly **higher** than Xiaomi (@tbl-brands, @fig-brand).
- **Motorola:** significantly **lower** than Xiaomi (1% level).
- **Oppo, Realme** and **other brands:** **not significantly different** from Xiaomi.
:::
::::
::::::

::: notes
Every brand comparison is against Xiaomi, the base category, for phones with similar specifications and features. So the brand gap is a brand premium, not a difference in hardware.
:::

## Summary of key findings

::: {.callout-important title="Key findings"}
1.  The six specifications reduce to **two components** that explain about **72%** of their variation: **overall performance (PC1)** and **storage and speed vs camera (PC2)**.
2.  **Both components**, **screen size**, **NFC** and **5G** are linked to significantly **higher** prices; **larger batteries** are linked to **lower** prices (@tbl-specs).
3.  **Brand matters beyond hardware:** with similar specifications, Apple, Samsung and Vivo are priced significantly higher than Xiaomi, Motorola is priced lower, and Oppo and Realme are not significantly different (@fig-brand).
:::

::: notes
Point 1 comes from the PCA; points 2 and 3 come from the regression.
:::

# Recommendations {background-color="#1f4e79"}

## Recommendation 1: performance

::: {.callout-note title="Finding"}
Overall performance (PC1) and the storage and speed focus (PC2) both have a **positive significant influence** on price at the 0.1% level, while battery capacity has a **negative** one (@tbl-specs).
:::

. . .

::: {.callout-tip title="Action for manufacturers"}
- To launch a **higher-priced model**, upgrade the **whole performance bundle**: processor, RAM, storage and refresh rate.
- Favour **storage and processing** over extra camera megapixels: storage- and speed-focused phones are priced higher than camera-focused ones.
- Use **large batteries** to add value to **budget models**, not to charge more.
:::

::: notes
This recommendation turns the two PCA components into a product design rule for manufacturers.
:::

## Recommendation 2: brand gap

::: {.callout-note title="Finding"}
With similar specifications, **Apple, Samsung and Vivo** are priced significantly **higher** than Xiaomi, while **Oppo and Realme** are not significantly different and **Motorola** is **lower** (@tbl-brands, @fig-brand).
:::

. . .

::: {.callout-tip title="Action for retailers and brands"}
- Display **Xiaomi** phones next to **Samsung and Vivo** models with matching specifications, and promote them as **"same specifications, lower price"**.
- **Motorola**, priced below Xiaomi, should compete on **specifications per price** rather than raise prices.
:::

::: notes
This recommendation uses the brand effects, which hold after controlling for specifications, so the gap is brand value rather than better hardware. Only Xiaomi is named in the display action because every brand coefficient is measured against Xiaomi.
:::
